subject: gl2bpp: ambiguity code for heterozygotes appended to the end of the sequence

messages.author: bfb3d90623cf316a
messages.subject: gl2bpp: ambiguity code for heterozygotes appended to the end of the sequence
parts:
Hi,

Used the gl2bpp function to export a sequence alignment using method = 1 to output IUPAC codes for heterozygotes. 

The output file however seems to append the IUPAC code to the end of the sequence (see attachment) instead of at the indicated position. The sequence length is 70 using method = 1 vs sequence length = 69 for method = 2 (heterozygotes resolved). Nucleotide 70 appears to be the SNP (T or C) with heterozygotes coded as Y.

Running dartR v 2.9.7, with  gl.install.vanilla.dartR(flavour = "dev").

Thanks,
Rachel

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: gl2bpp: ambiguity code for heterozygotes appended to the end of the sequence
parts:
Hi Rachel,

When working with DArTseq data and dartR, there are two possible definitions of SNP position.
1. Position of the SNP in the Trimmedsequence.
2. Position of the SNP in the chromosome/scaffold if you have your SNPs mapped to a reference genome. 

This position information can be stored in two different places:
1. In the slot "position" of the genlight object, for example: 
> platypus.gl$position
2. In the slot loc.metrics

By default, when dartR reads your DArT report, the SNP position of the trimmed sequence is stored in the slot "position"

The function gl2bpp uses the slot position to format the output file. 

In the dataset you sent me, you have in the slot "position" the SNP position of the reference genome. To fix this you could try:

> library(dartR)
> t1 <- gl.load("test.rds")
> t1$position <- t1$other$loc.metrics$SnpPosition
> gl2bpp(t1,outpath = getwd())

Cheers,
Luis
